# (Old) Loop 1.0.3 to 2.0.0 on CNAPP \- installation

**Installation steps for IBM Loop** 

In this document we will see the steps that are involved in installation of an IBM Loop instance in a new K8S environment.  
(Note: The steps are similar if you are trying to install a HCL version of Loop too.)

In this document we will be installing IBM Loop 1.0.3 on a CNAPP instance (10.190.116.49) 

**1\) Documentation link that was followed**

We used the CNAPP instance **10.190.116.49** for installing the IBM Loop 1.0.3 version.   
This VM had the K8S Cluster installed and configured on it.  
Following the IBM Documentation link that we overall followed for the installation steps:  
[https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=loop-installing-devops-kubernetes-service-k8s](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=loop-installing-devops-kubernetes-service-k8s)

**2\) Prerequisite scripts:**

We divided the steps in the documentation and put it into 3 separate scripts.  
The installation steps were divided into 3 separate scripts just for our convenience and re-usability.   
The 3 scripts are as below:  
\==  
root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\# ls \-ltr  
total 16  
\-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root  817 Jan  7 07:25 **prereq.sh**  
\-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root  549 Jan  7 07:26 **secrets.sh**  
\-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 5829 Jan  7 07:26 **ibm-loop-1.0.3-install.sh**  
root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\#  
\==

a) **prereq.sh** \- This script has the below commands grouped together which does all the prerequisite steps about \-\> adding the repos, helm update, installing emissary-ingress, getting the emissary related pods and the external IP

\==  
root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\# cat prereq.sh  
helm repo add datawire https://app.getambassador.io  
helm repo update

kubectl create namespace emissary && \\  
kubectl apply \-f https://app.getambassador.io/yaml/emissary/3.9.1/emissary-crds.yaml

kubectl wait \--timeout=200s \--for=condition=available deployment emissary-apiext \-n emissary-system

sudo mv /etc/cni/net.d/10-crio-bridge.conflist.disabled /etc/cni/net.d/10-crio-bridge.conflist

Perform the following step to create emissary-ports.yaml:  
*cat \<\<EOF \> emissary-ports.yaml*  
*service:*  
  *ports:*  
    *\- name: https*  
      *port: 443*  
      *targetPort: 8443*  
      *\#nodePort: \<optional\>*  
    *\- name: http*  
      *port: 80*  
      *targetPort: 8080*  
      *\#nodePort: \<optional\>*  
    *\- name: deploy-wss*  
      *port: 7919*  
      *targetPort: 7919*  
      *\#nodePort: \<optional\>*  
    *\- name: control-ssh*  
      *port: 9022*  
      *targetPort: 9022*  
      *\#nodePort: \<optional\>*  
*EOF*

helm install emissary-ingress \--namespace emissary datawire/emissary-ingress \-f emissary-ports.yaml && \\  
kubectl \-n emissary wait \--for condition=available \--timeout=90s deploy \-lapp.kubernetes.io/instance=emissary-ingress

kubectl get pods \-n emissary \-l app.kubernetes.io/instance=emissary-ingress

kubectl get nodes

kubectl patch service emissary-ingress \-n emissary \-p "{\\"spec\\": {\\"externalIPs\\": \[\\"$(hostname \-I | awk '{print $1}'  )\\"\]}}"

root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\#  
\==

b) **secrets.sh \-** In this script we have added the secret keys that are needed to access the IBM Entitled Registry.  
We also included the command to create a separate namespace and setting the context to the new namespace “devops-loop”.  
This ensures that we are running all the further installation related commands and steps in the same context.

\==  
root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\# cat secrets.sh  
kubectl create namespace devops-loop  
kubectl config set-context devops-loop \--namespace=devops-loop \--cluster=rajesh-a \--user=kubernetes-admin  
kubectl config use-context devops-loop

kubectl create secret docker-registry ibm-entitlement-key \\  
    \--namespace devops-loop \\  
    \--docker-username=cp \\    \--docker-password=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJJQk0gTWFya2V0cGxhY2UiLCJpYXQiOjE3NjA2MDMzNDgsImp0aSI6IjFkMWU2OTYwOGM1NjQxNjA4YjBiMWRiMzg1OTU0OGRlIn0.CIVVowHy3rH5pGqJjhZHjDmgnodyOUcNlQdfKdMaDT8 \\  
    \--docker-server=cp.icr.io

root@rajesh-a-control-plane:/loop-doc\#

\==

c)  **ibm-loop-1.0.3-install.sh \-**  The install script that we created by copying the installation code from the readme file from IBM Helm repo.  
Following is the command to fetch the Loop 1.0.3 installation readme file:  
\==  
\#Add the ibm helm repo  
helm repo add ibm-helm [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/charts/master/repo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/charts/master/repo)  
helm repo update

*helm show readme ibm-helm/ibm-devops-loop*  
\==

Note: If you are working on installing a different Loop version, make sure to refer the Loop product documentation link to use the command to pulling the corresponding Loop readme file and use it further for your installation purpose.

3\) Creating the install script from the Readme file from IBM Loop:  
After fetching the Readme file above, we created the **ibm-loop-1.0.3-install.sh** file by copying the contents of the readme file.   
Following is the example installation file that we created and used.  
Text that is highlighted in yellow are the values that we edited / added compared to the default Readme.md file.

\==  
\#Required  
\#External fully qualified domain name of the cluster  
\#  
\#See Installation of DevOps Loop documentation for more details:  
\#https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=installation-devops-loop  
INGRESS\_IP=10.190.116.49  
INGRESS\_FORWARDING=true

DOMAIN=${INGRESS\_IP}.nip.io

\#Required  
\#Set value to 'true' to accept the license.  
ACCEPT\_LICENSE=true  
\#SELF\_SIGNED=true

\#Required  
\#Hostname of IBM Rational license server  
LICENSE\_SERVER=10.134.59.129

\#Required  
\#SMTP Server configuration  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_HOST="email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_PORT="587"  
EMAIL\_FROM\_ADDRESS="root@hcl.com"

\#Optional  
\#Additional SMTP Server configuration  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_USERNAME="AKIARGIKQPM4G5XRMA"  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_PASSWORD="BJp2ra6O2kquocMZvRRIyvlVBelszgruXVB3QgMVh"  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_STARTTLS=false  
EMAIL\_SERVER\_SMTPS=false

\#Required  
\#Secure seed required to generate passwords  
\#A random string  
\#Unrecoverable so keep it safe  
PASSWORD\_SEED=secret

\#Specify the TLS secret name in your namespace as necessary.  
\#  
\#See Installation of DevOps Loop documentation for more details:  
\#https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=installation-devops-loop  
TLS\_CERT\_SECRET\_NAME=devops-loop-tls-secret

\#Set SELF\_SIGNED=true to generate and use a self-signed certificate for the  
\#installation of DevOps Loop  
SELF\_SIGNED=true

\#Alternative RWX storage class  
\#See Storage  
\#For example: ibmc-file-gold-gid  
RWX\_STORAGE\_CLASS=standard

\#Alternative RWO storage class  
\#See Storage  
\#For example: ibmc-block-gold  
RWO\_STORAGE\_CLASS=standard

\#Required  
NAMESPACE=devops-loop  
HELM\_NAME=devops-loop  
LOOP\_CHART\_VERSION=1.0.300

\#Optional Additional Helm options  
ADDITIONAL\_HELM\_OPTIONS=""

run\_install() {

  if \! kubectl get namespace ${NAMESPACE} \> /dev/null 2\>&1; then  
    kubectl  create namespace ${NAMESPACE} || { echo "Failed to create namespace"; return 1; }  
  fi

  if \! kubectl get secret mongodb-url-secret \--namespace ${NAMESPACE} \> /dev/null 2\>&1; then

    MONGO\_CHART\_VERSION="${MONGO\_CHART\_VERSION:-14.13.0}"  
    MONGO\_IMAGE\_TAG="${MONGO\_IMAGE\_TAG:-6.0}"  
    MONGO\_IMAGE\_REPO="${MONGO\_IMAGE\_REPO:-bitnamilegacy/mongodb}"  
    MONGO\_HELM\_RELEASE\_NAME="${MONGO\_HELM\_RELEASE\_NAME:-devops-loop-mongo}"  
    MONGO\_NAMESPACE="${MONGO\_NAMESPACE:-${NAMESPACE}}"  
    MONGO\_PVC\_SIZE=${MONGO\_PVC\_SIZE:-20Gi}

    helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami \--force-update 1\> /dev/null

    MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS="\\  
      \--set image.repository=${MONGO\_IMAGE\_REPO} \\  
      \--set image.tag=${MONGO\_IMAGE\_TAG} \\  
      \--set persistence.size=${MONGO\_PVC\_SIZE}  
    "

    if \[ \-n "${RWO\_STORAGE\_CLASS}" \]; then  
      MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS="${MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS} \--set persistence.storageClass=${RWO\_STORAGE\_CLASS}"  
    fi

    if \[ \-n "${MONGO\_ADDITIONAL\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS}" \]; then  
      MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS="${MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS} ${MONGO\_ADDITIONAL\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS}"  
    fi

    helm upgrade \--install ${MONGO\_HELM\_RELEASE\_NAME} \\  
      \--version ${MONGO\_CHART\_VERSION} \\  
      ${MONGO\_INSTALL\_OPTIONS} \\  
      \--namespace=${MONGO\_NAMESPACE} \\  
      \--create-namespace \\  
      bitnami/mongodb 1\> /dev/null || { echo "Failed to install MongoDB"; return 1; }

    MONGODB\_ROOT\_PASSWORD=$(kubectl  get secret \--namespace ${NAMESPACE} ${MONGO\_HELM\_RELEASE\_NAME}-mongodb \-o jsonpath="{.data.mongodb                                                      \-root-password}" | base64 \-d)

    MONGO\_URL="mongodb://root:${MONGODB\_ROOT\_PASSWORD}@${MONGO\_HELM\_RELEASE\_NAME}-mongodb:27017/admin"

    kubectl create secret generic mongodb-url-secret \--namespace ${NAMESPACE} \--from-literal=password="${MONGO\_URL}" 1\> /dev/null || {                                                       echo "Failed to create MongoDB secret"; return 1; }

  fi

  if \[ "${SELF\_SIGNED}" \= "true" \]; then  
    export TLS\_CERT\_SECRET\_NAME=devops-loop-tls-secret  
    openssl genrsa \-out key.pem 2048  
    openssl req \-new \-x509 \-key key.pem \-out cert.pem \-days 365 \\  
            \-subj "/CN=${DOMAIN}" \-addext "subjectAltName \= DNS:${DOMAIN},DNS:\*.${DOMAIN}" \\  
            \-addext "certificatePolicies \= 1.2.3.4"

    kubectl create secret generic ${TLS\_CERT\_SECRET\_NAME} \\  
      \--type=kubernetes.io/tls \\  
      \--from-file=ca.crt=./cert.pem \\  
      \--from-file=tls.crt=./cert.pem \\  
      \--from-file=tls.key=./key.pem \\  
      \--namespace ${NAMESPACE}  
  fi

  HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS:-} \\  
\--set global.domain=${DOMAIN} \\  
\--set-literal global.passwordSeed=${PASSWORD\_SEED} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.sender=${EMAIL\_FROM\_ADDRESS} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.host=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_HOST} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.port=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_PORT} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.username=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_USERNAME} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.password=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_PASSWORD} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.startTLS=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_STARTTLS} \\  
\--set global.platform.smtp.smtps=${EMAIL\_SERVER\_SMTPS} \\  
\--set global.ibmCertSecretName=${TLS\_CERT\_SECRET\_NAME} \\  
\--set global.persistence.rwxAccessMode=ReadWriteOnce \\  
\--set **ibm**\-devopsplan-prod.migration.rwx.enabled=false   
\--set license=${ACCEPT\_LICENSE}  
"  
**\#Note for the hcl version we need to use \--set hcl-devopsplan-prod.migration.rwx.enabled=false \\. This property is to be used only for cnapp instances**

  if \[ "${SELF\_SIGNED}" \= "true" \]; then  
     HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} \--set global.privateCaBundleSecretName=${TLS\_CERT\_SECRET\_NAME}"  
     HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} \--set ibm-devops-prod.ingress.cert.selfSigned=true"  
  fi

  if \[ \-n "${LICENSE\_SERVER}" \]; then  
    HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} \--set global.rationalLicenseKeyServer=@${LICENSE\_SERVER}"  
  fi

  if \[ \-n "${RWX\_STORAGE\_CLASS}" \]; then  
    HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} \--set global.persistence.rwxStorageClass=${RWX\_STORAGE\_CLASS}"  
  fi

  if \[ \-n "${RWO\_STORAGE\_CLASS}" \]; then  
    HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} \--set global.persistence.rwoStorageClass=${RWO\_STORAGE\_CLASS}"  
  fi

  HELM\_OPTIONS="${HELM\_OPTIONS} ${ADDITIONAL\_HELM\_OPTIONS}"

  helm upgrade \--install ${HELM\_NAME} ibm-helm/ibm-devops-loop \--version ${LOOP\_CHART\_VERSION} ${HELM\_OPTIONS} \\  
    \-n ${NAMESPACE} || return 1  
}

run\_install

\==

The key requirement is to create the installation script from the Readme file 

**4\) Installation execution:**

Reference URL for the installation steps:   
[https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=loop-installing-devops-kubernetes-service-k8s](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=loop-installing-devops-kubernetes-service-k8s)

a) Create a “emissary-ports.yaml” file with the following values:

\===========  
cat \<\<EOF \> emissary-ports.yaml  
service:  
  ports:  
    \- name: https  
      port: 443  
      targetPort: 8443  
      \#nodePort: \<optional\>  
    \- name: http  
      port: 80  
      targetPort: 8080  
      \#nodePort: \<optional\>  
    \- name: deploy-wss  
      port: 7919  
      targetPort: 7919  
      \#nodePort: \<optional\>  
    \- name: control-ssh  
      port: 9022  
      targetPort: 9022  
      \#nodePort: \<optional\>  
EOF

\===========

1) First run the “**prereq.sh**” script, does all the prerequisite steps about \-\> adding the repos, helm update, installing emissary-ingress, getting the emissary related pods and the external IP

2) 2nd run the “**secrets.sh**” \- which creates a separate Namesspace and adds the required Secrets.

3) 3rd run the “ **ibm-loop-1.0.3-install.sh**” \- which installs the Loop for us.

**5\) Monitoring the installation.**

We can use some of the below commands to monitor the Loops installation and to see which all PODs are coming up and what is the progress:

a) list the pods:  
kubectl get pods \-n devops-loop \-W

b) Describe the pods: \- to monitor and see if there are any errors in any of the PODs.  
kubectl describe pods \-n devops-loop \<pod-name\>

**6\) Creating the first set of user IDs to login to the LOOP:**

a) Access the Keycloak using the URL: [*https://10.190.116.49.nip.io/auth*](https://10.190.116.49.nip.io/auth)    
(Example:  https://\<fully-qualified-dns-name\>/auth/) 

b) Default user ID for keycloak is : “keycloak”  
Default password is: “66e91c191d4dd0e622a2ca9a3d06d62dba69a90179919c9446a854a860ae65f7” 

Note: Default password can be got using the below command:  
\==  
*kubectl get secret \-n devops-loop devops-loop-keycloak \-o jsonpath="{.data.password}" | base64 \--decode; echo*  
\==

c) Below link has the details about keycloack and user administration:  
[https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=administration-user-access-using-keycloak](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/devops-loop/1.0.3?topic=administration-user-access-using-keycloak)

**7\) Login to LOOP:**

 Once the user ID is created, you can access the LOOP application using the URL:  [*https://10.190.116.49.nip.io/*](https://10.190.116.49.nip.io/auth)*automation*   
(Example: https://\<fully-qualified-dns-name\>/automation)
